summary: Mark Juergensmeyer works in religious studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Illinois, Union Theological Seminary, Columbia University, and UC Berkeley (PhD 1974). His posts include UC Santa Barbara (~1993) and Claremont McKenna College.
Mark L. Blum is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. His career includes posts at the State University of New York at Albany, where he served as an associate professor (attested 2004–2006).

Mark McClish specializes in Indology and religious studies. A doctoral student of Patrick Olivelle, he held a post at Birmingham-Southern College and served on the editorial board of Anthem South Asian Normative Traditions Studies (both attested 2012).
Mark Owen works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Leeds under the doctoral supervision of Anna King and Elizabeth Stuart.

Indologist Mark S. G. Dyczkowski studied at Banaras Hindu University, Oxford (PhD ~1979 under Richard Gombrich and Alexis Sanderson), and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University. His traditional teachers included Swami Lakshman Joo, Kedar Raj Rajopadhyaya, and Rameshwar Jha.

Mark Siderits specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He served as Emeritus Professor of Philosophy at Illinois State University (~1978–2007) and at Seoul National University (~2007–2013).

Mark Singleton works in Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Cambridge and studied under Elizabeth De Michelis and Lakshmi Tatacharya. He was attested in 2020 as a Senior Research Fellow at SOAS.

Mark T. Unno works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. Educated at Oberlin College and Stanford University, he held posts at Brown University (~1998–2000) and the University of Oregon (~2000).

Mark Tatz was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his PhD from the University of British Columbia under Leon Hurvitz, studied under traditional teachers including Khenpo Appey Rinpoche, and served as professor at CIIS (attested 1988).

Mark Teeuwen specializes in Japanology and religious studies. He completed his MA and PhD at Leiden University, lectured at Cardiff University (1994–1999), and became a professor at the University of Oslo in 1999.
Mark Wilks was a scholar and colonial official in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Resident at the Kingdom of Mysore (~1803–1808) and Governor of Saint Helena (~1813–1816).

Markus Gabriel is a philosopher who studied at the University of Bonn. He has held appointments at Bonn (~2009), UC Berkeley (~2012), The New School (~2014), and became a Global Senior Advisor at the Kyoto Institute of Philosophy in 2024.

Markus Viehbeck specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Vienna (2012) under Helmut Tauscher and Franz-Karl Ehrhard, and has held posts at the University of Vienna and the University of Heidelberg.

Marsha Weidner specializes in sinology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After earning her PhD at UC Berkeley, she held art history posts at the University of Virginia (attested 1990) and the University of Kansas (attested 2001).

Marshall Sahlins was a scholar in history and archaeology. Educated at the University of Michigan and Columbia University, he taught at Michigan (~1957–1973) and the University of Chicago (from 1973).

Martha Nussbaum is a philosopher educated at Wellesley, NYU, and Harvard, who also studied under Bernard Williams. She held posts at Harvard, Oxford, and Brown before joining the University of Chicago in 1995 as a law and ethics professor.

Martin Baumann works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at Leibniz University Hannover and his Habilitation at the University of Leipzig, becoming a professor of religious studies at the University of Lucerne in 2001.

Martin Brauen is a Tibetologist and historian. Educated at Delhi and Zurich (PhD 1976), he held long-term curatorial posts at the Ethnographic Museum at the University of Zurich (from 1975) and served as chief curator at the Rubin Museum (2008–2012).

Martin Collcutt specializes in Japanology, history, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Cambridge and Harvard (PhD 1975), he taught at Tokyo and Yokohama National universities before serving as professor and East Asian Studies director at Princeton (1975–2015).

Martin Delhey works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto and Hamburg (PhD under Lambert Schmithausen) and has held posts at Hamburg, Göttingen, the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, Ryukoku University, and Shandong University (2019).
